mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where a team's recent-5 shots-for is elevated above its all-prior average while its recent-5 goals-for is simultaneously depressed below its all-prior average. Measure how often this joint divergence (high shots, low goals) co-occurs with a similarly divergent shots-on-target-to-shots ratio in the same window.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When recent shots-for rises above long-run average while recent goals-for falls below long-run average, the shots-on-target rate (shots_on_target / shots) is suppressed relative to the long-run ratio, indicating a conversion-quality deficit that is not visible from either observable in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume has risen sharply in recent matches while its goals-for has fallen sharply in the same window, suggesting a joint divergence between shot production and conversion efficiency. The relationship between Team A's recent shots-for and recent goals-for, measured jointly against their long-run averages, may reveal a suppressed conversion rate that is not captured by either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint relationship between two distinct observables (shots and goals) simultaneously diverging from their own baselines in opposite directions, then cross-referencing a third observable (shots_on_target). No single-observable mirror or single-band split captures this three-way joint state.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Pair Team A's shots_on_target FOR (recent-5 vs all-prior) against Team B's shots_on_target AGAINST (recent-5 vs all-prior), and simultaneously pair Team A's shots FOR against Team B's shots AGAINST. The conditioning is on the joint recent-form state of both teams across two distinct observables simultaneously.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's recent shots-on-target-for is elevated relative to its long-run level and Team B's recent shots-on-target-against is simultaneously depressed relative to its long-run level, the cross-team alignment is doubly favorable for Team A's attacking output — a reinforcing joint signal not present when only one side's observable is considered.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shots-on-target allowed has declined sharply in recent matches while its shots allowed has also declined, but the ratio of shots-on-target-against to shots-against may have shifted. Jointly measuring Team A's shots-on-target-for against Team B's shots-on-target-against (an asymmetric cross-team pairing of different observables) tests whether the attacking quality Team A generates aligns with or diverges from the defensive quality Team B concedes.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-team pairing: Team A's attacking observable is matched against Team B's defensive observable for the same metric, then both are simultaneously conditioned on their own recent-vs-long-run divergence. This is not a same-observable mirror (which uses one team's production vs the opponent's allowance at a single point in time without the joint recent-form conditioning across both).

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the half-level split jointly for both teams: compare Team A's corners-for in the first half vs second half against Team B's corners-against in the first half vs second half. The mechanism requires both the within-match half dimension and the cross-team asymmetry to be evaluated together.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: If Team A generates a disproportionately larger share of its corners in the second half while Team B concedes a disproportionately larger share of its corners in the second half, the corner advantage for Team A is amplified in the second half relative to what a full-match average would suggest — a half-level concentration effect not visible from full-match totals alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner-kick production is split asymmetrically across halves (first-half vs second-half), and Team B's corner-kick allowance is similarly split across halves. The joint within-match half-level profile of corner production for one team against corner allowance for the other — across both halves simultaneously — tests whether the corner advantage concentrates in a specific half rather than being uniform across the match.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on two dimensions: (1) within-match half (first vs second), and (2) the cross-team pairing of Team A's production against Team B's allowance at the half level. Neither a single-observable full-match mirror nor a single half-level split for one team alone captures this joint structure.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (1) Team B's goals-for split by half (first-half rate vs second-half rate relative to full-match rate), and (2) Team A's goals-against split by half (first-half rate vs second-half rate relative to full-match rate). The mechanism fires when both halves align — i.e., Team B front-loads its scoring and Team A front-loads its conceding in the same half.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's first-half goals-for rate is elevated relative to its second-half rate, and Team A's first-half goals-against rate is simultaneously elevated relative to its second-half rate, the first half represents a compounded vulnerability window — a joint half-level asymmetry that is suppressed or invisible in full-match averages.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Goals are split asymmetrically across halves for both teams. Team B scores a disproportionate share of its goals in the first half (goals-for first-half vs second-half), while Team A concedes a disproportionate share of its goals in the first half (goals-against first-half vs second-half). The joint half-level goal-scoring profile of Team B's attack against Team A's defensive half-level vulnerability tests whether a specific half represents a compounded risk window.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint evaluation of two distinct half-level splits across two teams for the same observable, where the direction of the asymmetry must align. A single team's half-level split, or a full-match mirror, does not capture this compounded within-match state.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the venue-specific joint state: use Team A's home possession-for and home fouls-for together, and Team B's away possession-for and away fouls-for together. The mechanism tests the cross-observable relationship (possession vs fouls) for each team in their venue role, then compares the two teams' joint profiles against each other.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the team with lower venue-specific possession (Team B away) also has a higher venue-specific foul rate relative to the team with higher possession (Team A home), the foul-count asymmetry between the two teams is positively associated with the possession asymmetry — a joint two-observable, two-team relationship that is not reducible to either observable's mirror alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's possession advantage (home) is paired with its fouls-for rate (home vs away), and Team B's possession level (away) is paired with its fouls-for rate (away). The joint relationship between possession share and foul rate — measured simultaneously across both teams in the venue-specific context — tests whether the team with lower possession commits more fouls, and whether this asymmetry is amplified or reversed at this specific venue configuration.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint relationship between two distinct observables (possession and fouls) evaluated simultaneously for both teams in their respective venue roles, then cross-compared. No single-observable mirror or single-band split captures the cross-observable, cross-team, venue-conditioned joint structure.
